phenomenon_scale.label: 4.1 µm
phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Dasypus novemcinctus (4.1 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.scale_contrast: Against the 273 µm primordium sibling, this 4.108 µm mode packs 66 wavelengths into 273 µm (remainder 1.872 µm). No chronospecies neighbour exists at a different age.

equations.kinetics: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u laplacian(u); dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v laplacian(v)
equations.dispersion: det(J - k^2 D) = D_u D_v k^4 - (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) k^2 + (f_u g_v - f_v g_u)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)

boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square dermal patch of side 12 * lambda_c. No-flux boundaries are not used.

parameter_table.note: D_u and D_v are solved from the critical-wavenumber formula so lambda_c equals 4.108 µm at this scale. They are not the sibling slot's parameters.

empirical_claims: Vickaryous and Hall (2006) describe five osteoderm shields in Dasypus novemcinctus; pectoral and pelvic shields carry hexagonal rosettes and the banded shield carries the movable bands.
Chen et al. (2011) measure mechanical and microstructural properties of the mineralized osteoderm, at a scale much coarser than 4.1 µm.

Turing (1952), Schnakenberg (1979), and Murray (1981) supply the dispersion relation and the coat-pattern interpretation. The 4.108 µm target is this loop's detail-scale rung, not a wavelength quoted by Chen or Vickaryous.
